2. In brief, the facts of the case are that during the investigation, the Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of eye-witness namely Irshad, which is reproduced us under: -
"I live with my family at the above address and I work as a labourer in a brick kiln.
Today we were going to Rohini in our vehicle to drop bricks.
I and the truck driver were present in this vehicle because more labour was coming in another vehicle.
Then when we reached before Barwala village, the driver of the vehicle Shyam Ray stopped the vehicle on the side to urinate.
I also went to the side to freshen up.
I came back and sat in the vehicle.
Then a truck came from behind.
At the same time our driver opened his window to get down.
Then that truck driver hit the driver side of the vehicle and caused an accident.
Then I got down from my vehicle and ran behind that truck.
That driver got down from the truck at some distance and ran away from there.

Then I came back to the vehicle and called my owner and told him that Shyam Ray has met with an accident caused by another truck driver and the truck Hiwa which caused the accident was standing there and the driver left the truck and ran away from there.
Then after this Shyam Ray was taken to MV Hospitals, Pooth Khurd Hospital for treatment and after that he was sent to another hospital for treatment due to the extent of his injuries.

Action should be taken against the truck driver who caused accident by driving his vehicle carelessly"

son of deceased, examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A.
Petitioners have also examined PW2, eye-witness of accident namely Irshad.
PW2 deposed that on 21.11.2018 at about 06:13 A.M he along with truck driver namely Shyam Ray were going from Durga Bhatta Company, Mohalla Majra towards Rohini.

When their truck reached before village Barwala.,
the driver of the truck stopped the truck for urinate and opened the door and he was in process of getting down from the truck in the meantime offending garbage truck/ trailer bearing No.
DL-1GB-6950 came from back side at a very fast speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Shyam Ray with great force.
Due to this forceful impact Shyam Ray crushed between offending truck and the truck which was driven by Shyam Ray and Shyam Ray sustained serious and grievous injures and died due to said injuries.
Though, PW2 has been duly cross examined by the respondent no. 2, however nothing material has come on record to disbelieve his testimony.

Further, PW2 has not at all been cross examined by the respondent no. 1 to prove that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that PWs are deposing falsely with regard to the involvement of vehicle in question or that SUNIL by SUNIL KUMAR Page no. 6 MACT No. 172/2022 KUMAR 03:39:55

Meaning thereby that they have nothing to say about the rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 and manner in which the accident had occurred as stated by PWs.

Though, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has also taken certain technical pleas in its written statement including the involvement of vehicle in question but neither any document has been placed on record nor any witness has been examined to prove such contention.

The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any evidence on such aspect.

Further, the criminal case record filed along with the DAR, which is collectively Ex.
PW1/2 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/304A IPC.
Apart from deposition of PWs, the fact that victim suffered fatal injuries in the accident is also supported by his postmortem report filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

"The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident "speaks for itself" or tell's its own story.

sentences.text: There are cases in which the accident speaks for itself so that it is sufficient for the plaintiff to prove the accident and nothing more.
It will then be for the defendant to establish that the accident happened due to some other cause than his own negligence.
Salmond on the Law of Torts (15th Ed.)

at p. 306 states: "The maxim res ipsa loquitur applies whenever it is so improbable that such an accident would have happened without the negligence of the defendant that a reasonable jury could find without further evidence that it was so caused."

In Halsbury's Laws of England, 3rd Ed., Vol. 28, at p. 77, the position is stated thus: "An exception to the general rule that the burden of proof of the alleged negligence is in the first instance on the plaintiff occurs wherever the facts already established are such that the proper and natural inference arising from them is ,that the injury complained of was caused by the defendant's negligence, or where the event charged as negligence "tells its own story' of negligence on the part of the defendant, the story so told being clear and unambiguous."

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh,
Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

entities.text: Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and victim suffered fatal injuries in the said accident

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Meaning thereby that they have nothing to say about the rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 and manner in which the accident had occurred as stated by PWs.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any evidence on such aspect.
Further, the criminal case record filed along with the DAR, which is collectively Ex.
PW1/2 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/304A IPC.
Apart from deposition of PWs, the fact that victim suffered fatal injuries in the accident is also supported by his postmortem report filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.
Relying upon judgment in Pushpabai Purshottam Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning & Pressing Co. (P) Ltd. & Anr. 1977 (2) SCC Lalita Devi (Wife Of Deceased Shyam Raj) vs Ram Awadh on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18468482/

Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and victim suffered fatal injuries in the said accident
However, as far as dependency is concerned as per judgment in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma and Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.
Civil Appeal No. 3483 of 2008 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 8648 of 2007) decided On: 15.04.2009 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Delhi, major son is not considered to be dependent on the income of deceased father.
12.As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 10% in case, the deceased was self employed and between the age of 50-60, at the time of accident.
As stated, the birth year of deceased was 1966,
which means that he was 52 years 10 months of age, at the time of accident.
Accordingly, a multiplier of 11 is thus taken for calculating loss of dependency.

. The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any evidence on such aspect.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.
